expectations.text: Produces the emergency plan as a document separate from the risk register, and says why - it is read under pressure by people, including volunteers, who never saw the register.
expectations.evidence: The plan is produced as its own document and the register is only a short extension. No reason is given for keeping them separate (read under pressure by people who never saw the register).

expectations.text: Writes a specific instruction for each named scenario rather than one general "safety incident" section.
expectations.evidence: Separate sections for Fire or smoke, Power failure, Medical emergency, Theft, and Evacuation for any other reason, each with numbered steps.

expectations.text: Covers fire in the venue, including evacuation route and assembly point.
expectations.evidence: "Evacuate to the assembly point: `[name the spot, upwind and away from the building and the road]`."

expectations.text: Covers electrical or power failure, including which circuits the event is actually overloading.
expectations.evidence: "map which circuits your power strips are on and distribute load across circuits."

expectations.text: Covers a medical emergency involving an attendee.
expectations.evidence: Medical emergency section: call the emergency number, meet the ambulance, named first-aider, AED.

expectations.text: Covers theft of equipment, naming attendee laptops and event networking or AV gear.
expectations.evidence: "180 people with laptops... theft target"; "Event gear (AV, network, printers) gets an inventory list".

expectations.text: Covers evacuation for any other reason, including who confirms the building is clear.
expectations.evidence: "A named person confirms with the venue or emergency services that the building is clear."

expectations.text: Does not rank or prioritise the named scenarios against each other, and states their ordering is set by the venue's own construction, the format and local emergency-services protocol rather than any value-per-effort calculation.
expectations.evidence: "These five are not ranked. Plan all of them, or state that the venue's own procedure owns one." It never says ordering is set by venue construction, format and local protocol.

expectations.text: Requires a physical printed copy on site, and says a plan living only in a shared drive fails at exactly the moment power loss, connectivity loss, dead phones or evacuation are what triggered the need for it.
expectations.evidence: "Print the plan... Digital-only fails when power, Wi-Fi or phones die."

expectations.text: Lists the non-emergency police line, explicitly labelled as distinct from the emergency number.
expectations.evidence: "Police non-emergency line (labelled separately; theft, disputes)".

expectations.text: Lists each lead organizer with the specific hours they will be on-site and reachable, not just a name and a number.
expectations.evidence: Contacts table: "Lead organizer 1 | | on-site hours:".

expectations.text: Requires at least one organizer awake and alert on site at all times for the full overnight duration, with a rota written in advance rather than improvised.
expectations.evidence: "One organizer awake and alert at all times... needs a written rota with named people, shift times and handover, made before the event."

expectations.text: Recommends notifying local emergency services in advance that a large event with many non-local attendees is running.
expectations.evidence: "Notify local emergency services in advance. Tell the local fire service and the police non-emergency line."
